slides.title: Starter Activity: 6-Cell Knowledge Retrieval

starterQuestions.q: Explain the three tiers of the 'Fact → Mechanism → Clinical Impact' writing framework.
starterQuestions.a: Fact: State the empirical finding/data; Mechanism: Explain the underlying cellular/physiological pathway; Clinical Impact: Explain the therapeutic outcome or prognostic consequence for patients.

starterQuestions.q: Why are personal pronouns (I, we, our) avoided in scientific academic writing?
starterQuestions.a: Passive and objective third-person syntax maintains scientific neutrality and focuses emphasis on the evidence rather than the investigator.

starterQuestions.q: What is an 'unfamiliar stimulus' in Level 3 AAQ assessments?
starterQuestions.a: Novel clinical data, experimental scenarios, or cutting-edge therapeutic trials not explicitly memorized from the specification, testing applied analytical skills.

starterQuestions.q: How should limitations of a clinical study be constructively framed?
starterQuestions.a: Identify the specific constraint (e.g. short follow-up duration), explain how it limits clinical generalisability, and propose targeted methodological refinement.

starterQuestions.q: What constitutes plagiarism in NEA coursework?
starterQuestions.a: Presenting another's ideas, text, figures, or synthesized arguments without explicit in-text citation and corresponding bibliography entry.

starterQuestions.q: What is the clinical role of bio-artificial organs in end-stage disease?
starterQuestions.a: Providing vital organ functions (e.g., hemodialysis, metabolic processing, cardiac assist) as a bridge to transplantation or permanent destination therapy.
